script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

---

Title: Unfrozen Hearts

Logline:
In the frigid heart of Alaska, two strangers, bound by a tragic past, must learn to forgive and heal in the face of overwhelming loss.

FADE IN:

INT. AIRPORT - NIGHT

A young woman, EMMA, bundled up against the cold, nervously waits for her ride. A car pulls up, and out steps a man, JACK, equally bundled up. They exchange greetings, awkwardly.

EMMA
(smiling)
I take it you're my ride?

JACK
(nods)
That's right. I'm Jack Thompson.

They get in the car, both uncomfortable in silence.

---

INT. JACK'S CABIN - DAY (2 DAYS LATER)

Emma sits at the kitchen table, staring at a photo of a family - Jack, his wife, and their little girl. Jack enters, a somber expression on his face.

JACK
I've told you about my wife, but not much about our daughter. Her name was Lily. She was four.

EMMA
(looking up, shocked)
I'm so sorry for your loss.

JACK
(sighs)
It's been four years, but it still feels like yesterday. I couldn't save her.

---

EXT. FOREST - DAY (3 DAYS LATER)

Emma and Jack go for a walk in the forest. They talk about their pasts, their regrets, and their dreams. Emma shares her story - how she lost her fiancé in a car accident and blames herself for not having married him earlier.

EMMA
I didn't know if I was ready, Jack. I thought I had more time.

JACK
(looking at her)
We never know when our time will run out. That's the cruel trick of life.

---

INT. JACK'S CABIN - NIGHT (5 DAYS LATER)

A power outage leaves them sitting in the dark, sharing stories by candlelight. Jack talks about the day Lily died and the guilt he feels for not being there when she needed him.

EMMA
(reaching out)
You were there in your heart, Jack. That's what matters.

Jack looks at her, surprised, and thanks her.

---

EXT. LAKE - DAY (7 DAYS LATER)

Emma and Jack sit by a frozen lake, watching the sunset. They share a moment of silence, each lost in their thoughts.

EMMA
(breaking the silence)
I've come to realize something, Jack. It's not fair to hold onto guilt and regret. We can't change the past, but we can learn from it and move forward.

JACK
(looking at her, a hint of a smile)
You're right, Emma.

---

INT. JACK'S CABIN - NIGHT (14 DAYS LATER)

Emma packs her bags, ready to leave. Jack sits in his chair, his eyes welling up with tears.

JACK
(sobbing)
I don't want you to go. You've helped me heal, Emma. You've given me a reason to live again.

EMMA
(smiling)
You've done the same for me, Jack.

They share a long, emotional hug, each knowing that they've found something precious in their time together.

---

EXT. AIRPORT - DAY (15 DAYS LATER)

Emma waves goodbye to Jack as he watches her board the plane. They exchange heartfelt words, knowing that their paths will cross again. As the plane takes off, Jack turns to face the cold Alaskan landscape, a sense of peace washing over him.

FADE OUT.

THE END
